solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A dance, it's associated with Latin South America

parts.note: 'it' is crossword slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA; the apostrophe-s is part of the surface

explanation.surface: A dance is described as having Latin American roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword convention; 'associated with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American partner dance, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Old Greek teacher in charge at Eton ignoring fashion, being refined fellow

parts.note: the sophists were paid teachers of rhetoric in ancient Greece

indicators.note: ignoring says these letters are left out of the words before

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style

explanation.surface: An Eton master steeped in the classics disdains fashion, yet is cultured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At Eton' minus TON leaves ATE. Eton is an elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophisticate is a worldly, cultivated person of refined tastes.

clue.text: In style, I will climb tree

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading upward, so the letters go backwards
In puts the letter I inside the word for style

parts.note: to style someone is to call them by a name

explanation.surface: Someone stylishly announces a plan to climb a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In style' looks like fashion, but 'style' is the verb meaning name.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a shrub or small tree with fragrant purple or white flowers.

clue.text: Slipshod palace guards quietly left one unaccompanied

indicators.note: guards says the jumbled letters surround the next piece
slipshod means careless, so these letters are put together sloppily in a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Careless palace guards slip away quietly, leaving one man alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing a cappella means performing with voices only, without instrumental backing.

clue.text: Sprinkle around a bit of liquid

definitions.text: Sprinkle around a bit of liquid

indicators.note: around says the sprinkling word goes round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to spatter is to sprinkle drops about

indicators.note: a bit of the word liquid is taken to be its opening letter only

explanation.surface: An instruction to scatter some drops of liquid about.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: to splatter is to sprinkle liquid around.
explanation.definitionFit: Splattering means splashing or spraying drops of fluid messily over an area.

clue.text: Cellist amended partly abandoned viola's part?

indicators.note: partly abandoned says most of these words are thrown away, leaving a run of their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cellist revises a viola line that was half dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'abandoned viola's part' as the definition, but 'abandoned' defines nothing; it joins 'partly' to signal the hidden word. Viola is also a flower, as in pansies.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-bearing male organ of a flower, and the viola is a flower genus.

clue.text: In Full Metal Jacket avoiding glum displays

definitions.text: In Full Metal Jacket avoiding glum displays

parts.words: In Full Metal Jacket avoiding glum displays
parts.note: the word glum without its outer letters, its jacket, shows LU, the chemical symbol of a metal; the clue asks for that symbol written in full

explanation.surface: A review of the Kubrick war film notes how it steers clear of gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'In full: metal (jacket avoiding glum) displays'. Strip G and M from glum to get the symbol LU, then give the element's whole name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutetium is a rare-earth metallic element with chemical symbol Lu.

clue.text: Chinese gangs that could make your hair curl?

definitions.text: that could make your hair curl?
definitions.meaning: curling irons are a heated tool for putting curls into hair

explanation.surface: Chinese criminal gangs are frightening enough to make your hair curl.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both Chinese criminal fraternities and a hairdressing tool for curling.

clue.text: Very conceited sort in prison shortly given comeuppance

indicators.note: in a down clue, come-up-pance hints that the letters come up, being read backwards
in says the word for shortly goes inside the prison

parts.note: a cage is a prison
in a mo means in a moment, shortly

explanation.surface: A vain person, soon jailed, gets what they deserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comeuppance' is split as 'come up': in a down light that reverses the letters, CAINAMOGE read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An egomaniac is someone obsessed with themself and their own importance.

clue.text: Sounds like you should assume cranky OAP's not fallen for trick

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so the scrambled letters take in the next piece
cranky means out of order or wonky, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; an OAP is an old-age pensioner

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to use a letter that is pronounced the same as the next word

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced exactly like the word you

explanation.surface: Someone is told to suppose that a bad-tempered pensioner hasn't been fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cranky' looks like a description of the pensioner but signals the anagram; 'should assume' puts the U (sounding like 'you') inside it. OAP (old-age pensioner) is everyday British for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a fast one on someone is an idiom meaning to deceive or con them.

clue.text: Tiny youngster's wise, we're told, about drug featuring in news broadcast

parts.note: a teen is a youngster, and teen's gives the letters with S

indicators.note: about says the two letters go around the following pieces
we're told signals that a word is heard rather than read

parts.note: said aloud, wise sounds like Y's, two letter Ys

indicators.note: featuring in says the drug letter goes inside the jumbled word
broadcast means scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A teenager's clever remark is heard on a TV news story about drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' heard aloud is 'Y's', a pair of Ys, which go 'about' E placed among the letters of NEWS ('broadcast').
explanation.definitionFit: Teensy-weensy is a childish reduplication meaning extremely small.

clue.text: Old copper is becoming investigator in episode's beginning

indicators.note: is becoming says one piece turns into another, replacing it in the word

parts.note: an episode is an incident; the apostrophe-s is a link
D is the abbreviation for an old penny, a copper coin in pre-decimal British money
PI stands for private investigator

explanation.surface: A retired policeman turns detective at the start of a TV episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old copper' suggests a former policeman, but it is the old British penny, a copper coin abbreviated d before decimalisation in 1971; 'is becoming' swaps it for the investigator.
explanation.definitionFit: Incipient describes something just starting to appear or develop, as in an incipient cold.

clue.text: Preposterously weeds look hard!

indicators.note: preposterous literally means back-to-front (before put after), so the last letter goes to the front

parts.note: tares are weeds that grow among corn, as in the biblical parable

explanation.surface: An exclamation of shock at how outrageous some weeds look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preposterously' is used in its Latin sense of 'hind part first': the final S of TARES moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare is to gaze fixedly and intently at something.

clue.text: Very little is drunk

definitions.meaning: a British colloquial word for tiny or minute
a British colloquial word for slightly tipsy

explanation.surface: Someone is barely drunk at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal British English both for something tiny and for being a bit tipsy.

clue.text: Revealing bust company's heading for liquidation, beset by strike

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so these pieces go inside the word for strike

parts.note: to strike out text is to delete it
CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of liquidation

explanation.surface: A financial report: the bust company is heading into liquidation, beset by strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like the bankrupt company, but belongs to the definition as in a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A décolleté dress has a low neckline that shows the neck and upper chest.

clue.text: Interrogate and search one that's charged

parts.note: a quest is a search
an ion is an atom or molecule carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Police procedure: grill and search a suspect who has been charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' points at a police charge, but it is electrical charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone is to interrogate them, asking them things formally.

clue.text: Movie mogul wants scorer on pitch? The reverse

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above another piece
the reverse says the order just described is swapped, putting pitch above the scorer

parts.note: a spiel is a sales pitch
Alban Berg was a composer, one who writes scores

explanation.surface: A film chief is after a goal-scorer on the football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer on pitch' suggests football; it is composer BERG over SPIEL, and 'The reverse' flips them.
explanation.definitionFit: Steven Spielberg is a hugely successful Hollywood film director and producer.

clue.text: For a start cedar's one, fir's another way to represent these

definitions.text: For a start cedar's one, fir's another way to represent these

indicators.note: for a start points to the opening letter of the word cedar
another way to represent means the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Cedar and fir are each examples of a group of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a cedar is one example, a fir another.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedars and firs are both cone-bearing evergreen trees, examples of the group.

clue.text: Australian native's to turn up to pool naked?

parts.note: to cock something, like a hat brim or an ear, is to tilt it upward
to and at are interchangeable in phrases like 'came to/at the door'

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of pool are removed

explanation.surface: An Australian seems to be planning a skinny-dip in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian native' suggests a person, but it is a bird; 'naked' strips P and L from 'pool'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockatoos are crested parrots found wild in Australia, so the bird is a native of that country.

clue.text: Bee hives can be so unpleasant

parts.note: the letter B is spelt out as bee
hives is a rash that makes the skin irritated and scratchy

explanation.surface: Beehives turn out to be nasty places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bee hives' reads as beehives, but splits into the letter B and the rash called hives.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitchy means spiteful or nasty in remarks about others.

clue.text: Rejection letter that's in your face

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the slang word for face

parts.note: dial is slang for a person's face
en is the name of the letter N, also a printing measure

explanation.surface: A letter of rejection is shoved right in someone's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence but is the letter N written as EN.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a refusal or rejection of a request or claim.

clue.text: Hat worn by daughter is a sign for Pedro?

indicators.note: a hat worn by someone sits around them, so this piece encloses the next

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A girl wears a hat as a signal to a Spanish man.
explanation.walkthrough: Pedro stands for any Spanish speaker: the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilde is the wavy mark over the n in Spanish, so it is a sign a Spaniard writes.

clue.text: Compound interest's adjusted, but not in time

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters are rearranged
but not says some letters must be taken away from the jumble

parts.note: taken as written; the apostrophe-s stands for is

explanation.surface: A financial note: compound interest is recalculated, though not on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound interest' reads as a phrase, but 'Compound' is the definition, a chemical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic chemical substance formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Doctrinaire guide ruined English tours round centre of Boulogne

indicators.note: tours means goes all the way round, so the scrambled letters enclose the next pieces
ruined says the letters of guide are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: the centre of Boulogne is its middle pair of letters

explanation.surface: A bossy tour guide in France gets everything wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' scrambles the guide's letters into IDEGU, which 'tours' (goes round) the circle and the centre of Boulogne; the English abbreviation comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrinaire person rigidly follows a theory; an ideologue is a zealous adherent of an ideology.

clue.text: New union member changes sides, causing dejection

indicators.note: changes sides means right becomes left, swapping the R for an L

parts.note: a groom is newly joined in the union of marriage

explanation.surface: A trade unionist defects, to the gloom of his comrades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but it is marriage; R (right) becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom is a state of sadness or low spirits.

clue.text: Allowed current feud finally to get personal in that, he's disappointed the others

parts.note: let means allowed

indicators.note: in that says the pronoun goes inside the current just named

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea
taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of feud

parts.note: one's own is personal to one

explanation.surface: A quarrel turned personal, and a team member failed his teammates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In that' puts the pronoun inside the current, the 'that' pointing back to it; the blogger found the clue a trifle contrived.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fail or embarrass one's team or group by poor behaviour or performance.

clue.text: Quiet gentleman back in Rio's ready for vengeful act

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the Brazilian money

parts.note: the real is Brazil's currency, cash in Rio; 'ready' is slang for money
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

indicators.note: back says the word for gentleman is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: sir is how a gentleman is addressed

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken gentleman back in Rio is primed to take revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for cash, so 'Rio's ready' is Brazilian money, the REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of retaliation against someone in return for harm done.

clue.text: Master entering school yard gets injured

indicators.note: entering says this letter goes into the other pieces

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
M is the abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster is hurt on the way into the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is a group of whales here, a gam, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammy is British informal for a leg or limb that is lame or damaged.
